items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'how are you today?', gave no agenda statement (what he'd cover / time estimate), and never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
2_probe: Never captured the origin zip code, never asked about moving stressors/worries, and never asked about additional stops along the route.
3_pricing: No 'pricing is super simple' opener, and Meet Your Mover was never mentioned.
4_clock: Didn't explain the 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, and skipped a sense-check ('does that make sense?').
5_estimate: Didn't tie stairs, specialty items, walk distance, traffic, or an equivalents reference (e.g. school bus) into the estimate as time variables.
6_save_your_ass: Entire prep speech skipped — no 'prep shortens the move' framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no close.

7_quote_booking: Didn't mention the bolded detail list at the top of the email, didn't ask the customer to reply with corrections, skipped 'any other questions before I let you go,' and never gave hours or how to reach the office.
8_politeness: Addressed the customer as 'sir' almost the entire call — used his actual name ('Sona') only once, while confirming the email spelling.
9_bonus: No rapport-building or humor moments, and the insurance pitch covered the $2,000 coverage but skipped the 60-cents-per-pound baseline comparison.
top_strength: Arden ran a tight, thorough intake — origin and destination addresses, floors, parking access, and inventory were all captured methodically — then delivered pricing that held up under real-time math: "I'm estimating the move to take around three to three and a half hours, sir. So it's good to budget an overall of $852 for the move," and proactively covered no-hidden-fees, damage coverage, and the on-time guarantee before the customer had to ask.
coaching_note: You skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely — that's the highest-value section for shortening a move and it cost you 10 points here. Open with a real agenda statement ("I'll grab some details, then walk you through pricing, takes about 10 minutes, sound good?") instead of jumping straight into questions, and use the customer's name instead of defaulting to "sir" — you said "Sona" exactly once on an 8-minute call. Before you hang up, always ask "any other questions before I let you go?" and give him the office hours and how to reach you so he's not left guessing.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient throughout — repeated pricing details without frustration when asked — but the call is entirely task-driven with no affirmations, empathy statements, or acknowledgment beyond restating information.
